papers.version_note: arXiv:2312.10779v1 [math.QA] 17 Dec 2023. The text layer garbles the abstract's square-root sign and some displayed formulas; assertions that depend on those formulas are stated in words and quote only the legible text.
papers.what_it_is: A mathematical-physics paper on noncommutative (quantum) Riemannian geometry of graphs: it builds quantum Levi-Civita connections on n-leg star graphs and derives and numerically solves quantum geodesic flow equations on the 4-star graph and on the integer line.

assertions.value: The authors state that they revisit the construction of quantum Riemannian geometries on graphs starting from a hermitian metric compatible connection, which always exists.
quotes: We revisit the construction of quantum Riemannian geometries on graphs starting
from a hermitian metric compatible connection, which always exists.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the approach the paper takes.

assertions.value: The paper states that a left connection written as nabla e_i = minus Gamma_ij tensor e_j, for a form-valued matrix Gamma, is hermitian-metric compatible if and only if dg + Gamma g + g Gamma dagger = 0, where g is the A-valued matrix of the hermitian metric.
quotes: is hermitian-metric compatible if and only if
dg + Γg + gΓ† = 0
assertions.certainty_reason: The condition is recalled from the cited text [4, Chap. 8.3]; no proof is given in this paper.

assertions.value: The paper states, citing a theorem from the literature, that if the calculus is inner then a left bimodule connection has the form nabla omega = theta tensor omega minus sigma(omega tensor theta) plus alpha(omega) for some bimodule maps sigma and alpha.
quotes: if Ω1 is inner, then a left bimodule connection has the specific form
∇ω = θ ⊗ ω − σ(ω ⊗ θ) + α(ω)
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited theorem ([15] and [4, Thm 8.11]), not proved in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not necessarily impose quantum symmetry, sigma-symmetry or edge-symmetry on the metric, so they work with nondegenerate generalised metrics.
quotes: We do not necessarily impose any of these, i.e. we are more precisely working with nondegenerate ‘generalised metrics’.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope.

assertions.value: The paper presents quantum geodesics as a flow of geodesics: the tangent vectors form a geodesic-time dependent vector field X(t) obeying the geodesic velocity equation X dot plus nabla_X X = 0 (classically), and a wave function psi obeys the amplitude flow equation psi dot plus kappa psi plus X(d psi) = 0, with kappa equal to one half of the divergence of X.
quotes: we do not think
about one geodesic at a time but rather a flow of geodesics much like in fluid dynamics
ψ˙ + κψ + X(dψ) = 0,
assertions.certainty_reason: These are the defining equations of the framework as set out in the introduction (originating in the cited works [3, 7, 8]).

assertions.value: The authors state that one new feature of this work is to allow an imaginary driving force F on the right hand side of the quantum version of the geodesic velocity equation, which can alternatively be used to maintain unitarity of the amplitude flow; their previous auxiliary condition now appears as F = 0.
quotes: is to further generalise this set-up by allowing an imaginary driving force F on the right hand
amplitude flow (our previous auxiliary condition now appears F = 0).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states what it adds beyond earlier work.

assertions.value: The paper requires the geodesic velocity field and kappa at each geodesic time to obey two unitarity conditions, one of which says X is real with respect to the integral, and states that the amplitude flow equations then keep the integral of psi star psi constant in time, as needed for a probabilistic interpretation.
quotes: We do require that the geodesic velocity field and κ at each s to obey the unitarity conditions
The above conditions ensure that ∫ ψ∗ψ is constant in time, which is needed for a probabilistic interpretation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The claim is stated without proof in this paper and is attributed to the framework of [8].

assertions.value: The authors state that it is not automatic that a velocity field X that is initially real with respect to the integral stays real under the geodesic velocity equation; they impose this as an improved auxiliary equation, or else add an imaginary driving force F chosen to maintain reality.
quotes: It is not automatic that if Xs is initially real with respect to ∫ that it
necessarily remains so under the geodesic velocity equation
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this as a limit of the framework in Section 2.2.

we exclude self-arrows and multiple arrows.

assertions.value: The paper states that one can set alpha equal to zero, so that full torsion freeness and star-preservation hold for such inner connections as soon as they are torsion-compatible and star-compatible, and that a torsion free, star-preserving connection is then metric compatible in the usual non-hermitian sense, i.e. a quantum Levi-Civita connection.
quotes: one can set α = 0 so full torsion and ∗-preserving hold for these such inner connections as soon as they are torsion and ∗-compatible.
it is metric compatible in the usual (non hermitian sense) also, i.e. a QLC.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in Section 3 as following from the cited general results on inner calculi.

assertions.value: The paper states, as a theorem, that for the n-star graph hermitian-metric compatible and star-compatible connections exist only if a fixed ratio condition between lambda_{0 to i} and lambda_{i to 0} holds (the text layer garbles the formula), that such connections are necessarily star-preserving with alpha equal to zero, and that with the minimal calculus the torsion free ones, which are the moduli of quantum Levi-Civita connections, exist only for n at most 4.
quotes: hermitian-metric compatible and ∗-compatible connections exist only if
and are necessarily ∗-preserving with α = 0. Using Ωmin, torsion free such connections are the moduli of QLCs and exist only for n ≤ 4.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3.4 is stated with its conditions and proved in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state in the abstract that, as for the A_n Dynkin graph, the metric length for each outbound arrow has to exceed the length in the other direction by a multiple, here a square root of n (the root sign is lost in the text layer).
quotes: outbound arrow has to exceed the length in the other direction by a multiple, here n.
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from the first condition of Theorem 3.4, which is proved in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that for n = 2 the moduli of connections has a free phase parameter, for n = 3 there is a unique choice of a phase or its conjugate (two connections), and for n = 4 there is a unique connection corresponding to phase -1.
quotes: For n = 2 the moduli of connections has a free phase parameter. For n = 3, there is a unique choice of a phase
or its conjugate (two connections) and for n = 4 there is a unique connection corresponding to phase -1.
assertions.certainty_reason: A summary of Theorem 3.4 parts (a) and (b), proved in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors report that the remaining relations needed for the star-graph solutions can be checked to hold for n = 3, 4 and fail for n at least 5.
quotes: These can be checked to hold for n = 3, 4 and fail for n ≥ 5.
assertions.certainty_reason: The check is stated without its working in the proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that more star-preserving solutions, for example for larger n, could potentially exist if the minimal calculus is quotiented further so that being torsion-free is less restrictive.
quotes: We can potentially have more ∗-preserving solutions, e.g. for larger n, if we quotient Ωmin further so that being torsion-free is less restrictive.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its own non-existence result.

assertions.value: The authors state that the n = 2 star graph case is the same as the A3 Dynkin graph treated in earlier work [2], that the constraints on the ratios of inbound and outbound metric coefficients are the same as found there, and that they obtain exactly the same connection with s = s1 as the free modulus parameter.
quotes: The n = 2 case is the same as the A3 Dynkin graph
We also obtain exactly the same connection ∇ as in [2] with s = s1 as the free modulus parameter found there.
assertions.certainty_reason: A comparison with a cited earlier result, stated without the working.

assertions.value: The paper states for n = 2 more general solutions with s1 a free phase parameter and s2 obtained from s1 by a Mobius transform that maps phases to phases and has the special values of case (a) as its fixed points.
quotes: Here, s1 is a free phase parameter and s2 is obtained from s1 by a M¨obius transform that maps phases to phases
assertions.certainty_reason: Part (b) of Theorem 3.4, proved in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the integer line with generators plus and minus one and an edge-symmetric metric they use the unique star-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connection from earlier work [1], with nabla e_pm equal to (1 minus rho_pm) e_pm tensor e_pm, and that it also descends to Z_n, which has a unique star-preserving QLC when n is not 4.

assertions.certainty_reason: A result cited from [1] and used here without proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that for Z_n with n = 4 and the smaller calculus there are some further star-preserving QLCs, and that it is not known if there is a unique QLC for n = 4 if the bigger calculus is used.

assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states an open question.
